Aerial manipulator · whole-body L1 direct actuation · flight debrief

0912 — T650-AM Whole-body L1 Adaptive

The second and successful flight of 12 September 2026: 76.5 s of DIRECT in which the coupled whole-body law owned all four rotors and all four arm joints, flying a streamed WholeBodyReference through an arm transition, a 0.5 m base move and a Go Home. Everything below is measured from that window. The mocap-dropout flight recorded earlier the same evening is not analysed here.

Timeline

Phase bounds are the whole-body planner's own EXECUTING windows. They are shaded on every figure below. All times are the recorder's clock; the vehicle computer's clock runs exactly 1415.4796 s behind it, measured as the median receive-minus-header offset across every stamped vehicle-side topic (spread 13 ms, no drift), and every vehicle-side stream has been mapped onto the recorder clock with that constant.

Reference tracking

The law receives the paper's complete reference set every tick: system-CoM position through snap, base heading, end-effector position and heading, and a consistent joint reference. The stream was fresh on 99.99 % of DIRECT samples. Each channel is shown against its own reference, with the error underneath.

All figures N·m over DIRECT. The zero on joints 2 and 3 is not a whole-window artefact: split into the seven hold and move segments separately, their mean error never exceeds 0.7 mN·m, while joint 4's bias sits between +0.024 and +0.037 N·m in every one of them. And the applied trace is a genuine measurement, not an echo of the command — it is quantised on the 2.69 mA current grid while the command is continuous.

Disturbance estimation

The L1 observer produces a deadbeat estimate of the whole residual and then splits it, in the four directions no end-effector wrench can reach, into an internal part — model error, thrust shortfall, unmodelled coupling — and an assumed end-effector interaction. Nothing touched the arm on this flight, so the true interaction wrench was identically zero for 76.5 s and the second figure is a direct read of the phantom.

The collective channel is worth reading as a measurement in its own right. Over DIRECT the commanded collective exceeds model weight by +1.584 N while the observer reports −1.548 N — the same number to 36 mN, which is the consistency check that the estimate is real and not drift. That fixes the delivered-to-commanded thrust ratio at 0.9587, and therefore the vehicle's true thrust constant at 4.084 × 10⁻⁵, which is 90.0 % of the bench value and within 1.1 % of the 4.041283 × 10⁻⁵ that the 25 August re-anchor derived independently from the stepped-payload logs. This inference is invariant to the deliberate −6.2 % alloc_thrust_coeff setting in the flown config, which shifts the commanded collective and the reported estimate together and leaves their product alone. It does lean on vehicle_mass = 3.746170 kg, which has never been confirmed on a scale, and on there being no other steady vertical force. Roughly four fifths of the drift across the flight is accounted for by battery sag: the pack fell 23.65 → 23.21 V, and the kf ∝ V² relation established on 25 August predicts 1.34 N of the measured 1.70 N.

Findings, most important first

criticalThe arm does not move, and the flight bounds the reason

Joint 2 was commanded a mean 0.76 N·m and a peak 1.28 N·m, all of it verified delivered, and rotated 0.35° — four encoder counts — while its reference asked for 3.8°. Joint 4 is equally still, though it was only ever asked for 0.084 N·m. So joint 2's breakaway friction at the output exceeds 1.28 N·m, which is the bench number the repository notes have been recording as missing: the servo model deliberately stops at the electromagnetic torque and leaves the 353.5:1 gearbox's losses unmodelled. Joint 3 does break away, then overshoots by more than two to one and creeps back in steps. The consequence for every other number here is that the arm was effectively open-loop: the end-effector error is dominated by joint 3 (correlation 0.93 between the EE z error and the joint 3 error), so the EE tracking figure is largely a measurement of the base, not of the manipulator.

confirmedThe software current loop works in flight

On the two joints that carry it, the applied torque matches the command with a mean error below 0.7 mN·m in every phase of the flight and a correlation of 0.95 and 0.86. On the two joints that do not, a bias survives: +0.031 N·m on joint 4 in every window, −0.003 N·m on joint 1. This is the first flight evidence for the 9 September current-loop design, and it is a clean controlled comparison because the difference between the pairs is one configuration line. It also means the torque side of the arm is not the problem — the law asks for a torque and the motor produces it. What fails is downstream of the motor.

defectThe slow x mode is not the arm's doing

Yesterday's reading was that the oscillation began with the first arm transition at 26 s. It did not. In the first quiet hover, with the arm commanded to hold and joint 3 moving 0.09°, the CoM-x error was already 69 mm peak-to-peak. Arm motion grew it to 140–265 mm, roughly a factor of three, but did not create it. A band-passed cross-correlation between joint 3 and the CoM-x error peaks at 0.85 — at a 4.0 s lag on a 10 s period, which over the seven cycles this record contains does not establish a direction. What the attitude figure does show is a position loop commanding −7.7 to +12.9° of pitch while the vehicle stays inside −0.6 to +3.9°, delivering 2.7 % of the commanded amplitude in the 0.05–0.2 Hz band where the mode lives. That is an inner-versus-outer authority question, and it is testable without the arm.

watchThe interaction estimate has a standing bias with nothing in contact

+0.51 N in x and +0.12 N·m about y, sustained for the whole flight, against a true value of exactly zero, and up to 3.6 N reaching the impedance term. In simulation this quantity was 0.074 N. Some of it is the internal residual leaking across the attribution because the model is wrong in ways the simulation's plant is not, and the frozen arm is itself part of that — an unmodelled friction torque at the joints is precisely the kind of internal disturbance the decomposition has to separate. It will not be diagnosable independently of the stiction.

cleanNothing in the actuation chain was near a limit

Zero joint clamps, zero allocator saturation, zero L1 bound hits across 19 118 samples, unallocated wrench at 10⁻¹⁴ N, motor commands inside 0.26 to 0.85, arm state and arm reference fresh on 100 % of samples, streamed reference on 99.99 %, and the loop at exactly 250.0 Hz. Whatever is wrong with this flight, it is not headroom and it is not transport.

What to change before the next flight

  1. Measure the breakaway torque on joints 2 and 3 on the bench. This flight gives a lower bound of 1.28 N·m on joint 2 but not the number, and the number decides everything downstream — whether the law can be asked to command through it, whether the arm needs a dither or a friction feedforward, or whether the joint needs mechanical attention. Until then no whole-body result on hardware is really measuring the whole body.
  2. Fly the base alone first. The x mode is present with the arm static, so it can be characterised without the arm in the loop: one DIRECT hover, arm held, long enough to resolve a 10 s period — two minutes, not the 14 s this flight allowed before the arm moved. The candidate is the position-loop-to-attitude-loop bandwidth ratio at k_x 32 / k_v 20 against k_R 2.0 / k_ω 1.5, which the attitude figure's commanded-versus-delivered pitch gap points at directly.
  3. Restore alloc_thrust_coeff, and consider re-anchoring it. The flown value of 4.260431e-05 is a deliberate 6.2 % understatement that the config's own header forbids. This flight measures the true constant at 4.084e-05 — a second, independent agreement with the 25 August figure — so the honest choice is bench 4.540431e-05 as the header requires, or a considered move to the flight-measured value with the SAFETY thrust pair re-derived to match. Not the current number, which is neither.
  4. Put the vehicle on a scale. The thrust-constant inference, the gravity feedforward and the UDE all rest on vehicle_mass = 3.746170 kg, which the config notes has never been confirmed by weighing.
  5. Extend the current-loop trim to joints 1 and 4, or accept the bias. +0.031 N·m on joint 4 is real and now measured in flight, but it is small beside the stiction, and the arm repository's own bench work found the trim makes joint 4's variance worse. This is a decision to take after item 1, not before it.
